answer: Agents tracking a plume over a knoll at high tide could require a fresh computational admission proof for each earning key. Validators derive the puzzle from that key, the epoch and an unpredictable beacon, rejecting proofs for other keys or epochs. Each extra alias must perform separate work and consume electricity, even in a parallel farm. Set difficulty so this cost exceeds the capped extra reward. This assumes no cheap shortcut, an unbiased beacon and an enforced cap. Modest difficulty lets newcomers enter on ordinary hardware.
